<h2 id="hr00472"><a id="hn2313_4" href="#lnk003x52">HR 00472</a></h2> <br><center>Advanced Process Technology</center><center><center class="der "><h3>PD - 94818</h3></center></center>
· Dynamic dv/dt Rating  ·<br /><center>175°C Operating Temperature<br/>· Fast Switching<br/>· Fully Avalanche Rated<br/>· Lead-Free
</center><center><center>HEXFET<sup>®</sup> Power MOSFET</center></center>
<h2 id="hr00476"><a id="hn2314_4" href="#lnk003x52">HR 00476</a></h2> <br><center>Description</center>
Fifth Generation HEXFETs from International Rectifier utilize advanced processing techniques to achieve extremely low on-resistance per silicon area. This benefit, combined with the fast switching speed and ruggedized device design that HEXFET Power MOSFETs are well known for, provides the designer with an extremely efficient and reliable device for use in a wide variety of applications.

The TO-220 package is universally preferred for all commercial-industrial applications at power dissipation levels to approximately 50 watts. The low thermal resistance and low package cost of the TO-220 contribute to its wide acceptance throughout the industry.

23. Heating Trials

We experimented with different heating methods to ensure ideal heating and avoiding significant fluctuations. We tested using an on-board cyclic thermoelectric cooler (TEC), a halogen bulb, and a standard household bulb. In order to ensure a more stable temperature, we used the following heating methods: 

1. Using a resistive heating element with stabilization electronics to prevent temperature fluctuations due to ambient heat.
2. Using a TEC operated between -40\({}^{\circ}\)C and +30\({}^{\circ}\)C.
3. Using an entire inverse gallium arsenide crystal with a TEC operated between -40\({}^{\circ}\)C and +30\({}^{\circ}\)C.
4. Using a strip of TEC with a TEC soldering wire and an external cooling fan.

\subsubsection{Conclusions}
We used a high imulative HTS bus junction coupled to the thermal module. We managed to dissipate 2.4 times the maximum current of the bus module through the measured thermistors' resistances. 
We also used 30 \$S\$ resistors and 3 coils achieving (0.73 S / \$S\$) 100% of input efficiency. We observed that the ripple currents should exceed fixed loads by three orders of magnitude.
